numbering_direction.summary: Section numbers INCREASE from right field, around the first-base side, past home plate, along the third-base side, and out to left field. In other words, numbers rise toward third base / left field and fall toward first base / right field. Low 100s = right field bleachers; mid 140s-150s = behind home plate; high 160s-190s = left field. Viewed from above with home plate at the bottom of the map, the numbers run clockwise (RF -> 1B -> HP -> 3B -> LF). The same direction holds on the 200, 300 and 400 levels.

accessibility.summary: Wheelchair-accessible and companion seating is distributed on every level; the official Cardinals Access Guide for Guests with Disabilities identifies accessible seating by its proximity to elevators, escalators and ramps rather than by a full section list. Eligible patrons may purchase up to THREE companion tickets in adjacent seats. Accessible seating is sold by phone at (314) 345-9000 or at the Ticket Windows on 8th Street near Gate 3. Every gate at Busch Stadium is accessible. Wheelchair escorts are available on request, service dogs are welcome, and assistive listening devices are available at Guest Relations on Level 1 at Section 148. Note that many 100-level infield sections carry a 'WC' row (for example section 146 lists 'Rows 1-19, WC'), which is the wheelchair platform row at the back of the section, at the concourse entrance.

discovery.row_seat_conventions: ROWS: predominantly NUMBERS, but the field-level infield uses a MIXED scheme - lettered rows closest to the field followed by numbered rows behind a cross-aisle walkway. Confirmed example: Section 141 rows are labeled 'F-L, 1-24' with a walkway separating row L from row 1, so row F is the front row and row 1 sits BEHIND row L. Other confirmed examples: section 150 rows 1-26; section 146 rows 1-19 plus a 'WC' (wheelchair) row at the entrance; section 350 rows 1-6; section 442 rows 1-11; section 372 rows 1-14; bleacher section 101 rows 1-13. In numbered-row sections, row 1 is closest to the field and the highest row is at the concourse entrance. SEATS: the consistent park-wide rule per RateYourSeats is 'when looking towards the field, LOWER NUMBERED SEATS ARE ON THE RIGHT' - i.e. seat 1 is on the RIGHT as you face the field, and seat numbers increase to the LEFT. Confirmed on sections 101, 141, 146, 150 and 350. Seat counts per row vary within a section (e.g. section 442: rows 1-4 have seats 1-19, row 5 has 1-22 with seats 20-22 above the entry tunnel, row 6 has 1-19, rows 7-10 have 1-24, row 11 has 1-25). CONFIRMED.
discovery.known_obstructions: 1) PROTECTIVE NETTING: extended safety netting runs in front of roughly sections 142-158 on the field level (the full infield arc from dugout to dugout), so behind-the-plate and dugout-box seats view the game through the net; RateYourSeats reviewers generally report it does not spoil the experience. 2) UNDERHANG / OVERHANG: on the 100 level, the back rows sit under the deck above - at section 150 rows 24+ are covered, at section 146 the rearmost rows are covered; the overhang cuts off the top of the sky and can hide high fly balls and portions of the video board. Similar coverage lines exist on the upper decks (section 442 rows 4+, section 372 rows 8+ are covered). 3) TUNNEL/ENTRY seats: some rows have extra seats sitting above an entry tunnel (e.g. section 442 row 5 seats 20-22), giving an offset sightline. 4) BLEACHERS: the odd-numbered outfield bleachers (101-111, 189-197) are benches with minimal shade and look in from beyond the fence; sections above the bullpens can have the bullpen mounds and railings in the near foreground. 5) CONCERTS: for non-baseball events, low right-field sections such as 101 sit behind or beside the stage. 6) UPPER RIGHT FIELD: sections 431-435 are the farthest, most sun-exposed seats in the park. MOSTLY CONFIRMED via RateYourSeats section pages 146, 150, 156, 101, 442, 372, 431; no fixed support columns/poles were reported at this ballpark (it is a modern 2006 cantilevered design).
